summary: npm package ships only a disguised Cloudflare-challenge HTML page with an obfuscated client-side redirect
details: The package contains only package.json and index.html; there are no lifecycle scripts and main points at the HTML file, so installing or requiring the package does not execute code on the installer. The shipped index.html impersonates a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interstitial (fake dynamically-generated Ray ID and Cloudflare branding) and, after a 1-second timeout, runs obfuscator.io-style code (rotated string-array `_0x3b86`, `_0x`-named accessor, self-defense IIFE, console-hardening IIFE) that assembles a redirect URL whose only plaintext fragment is `https://lo`, copies the incoming query parameters onto it, and navigates `window.location` to the assembled destination. The pattern (fake-Cloudflare cover page + heavily obfuscated destination + query-param passthrough) is characteristic of phishing/malvertising landing pages hosted via public npm CDNs such as unpkg or jsdelivr. The victims of this abuse are web visitors who load the HTML through an npm CDN URL, not developers who install the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
